tagline: The old timber road along Tahoe's Nevada shore.
intro: From Stateline the byway takes US 50 north along Lake Tahoe's east shore, past Zephyr Cove and Glenbrook, and at Spooner Junction, just south of Spooner Lake, turns onto SR 28. For a few miles it runs inland through national forest and state park. Then it comes back to the shore for about four miles by Sand Harbor and goes on through Incline Village to Crystal Bay at the California line.
It was a timber road before it was a highway. Flumes ran along it from 1880, carrying wood toward the Comstock mines, and the pavement came around 1932.

moments.title: Glenbrook
moments.text: The oldest settlement on the lake had four sawmills in 1875, cutting timber for the Comstock. The logging was gone by 1900, and the beach now belongs to the residents.

moments.title: Sand Harbor
moments.text: Logs cut around the lake were once towed into this harbor behind the steamship Niagara. In July and August the Lake Tahoe Shakespeare Festival plays here.

moments.title: Incline Village
moments.text: The town is named for an incline railway that hauled timber 1,400 feet up the mountain to a flume, which sent it down the far side toward Carson City.

practical: Sand Harbor requires day-use reservations for morning vehicle entry from May 15 through September 30, and stopping along Highway 28 outside designated parking will not get you in.
